speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Given your history of AIDS and symptoms of decreased vision and black spots in the right eye, I suspect an opportunistic infection. Can you tell me if these black spots float or move across your vision like flies?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history of Kaposi's sarcoma and esophagitis raises concern for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis; do you see these black spots as streaks or patches of color change rather than just floating dust?

REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy
REQUEST IMAGES: Right_eye_retina_photos

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text: The findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages in your retina are highly characteristic of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis, a common opportunistic infection in AIDS patients. Do you recall if you have had any recent fevers, chills, or a change in your CD4 count since your last appointment?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis

The clinical presentation of painless vision loss with "black spots," combined with your history of AIDS and the specific fundoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages, confirms the diagnosis of CMV retinitis.
